This anticipatory bail application under Sections 482 and 484 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita has been preferred by the petitioner apprehending his arrest in connection with C.I.D. P.S. Case No.51 of 2024, registered for offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420, 34 of the Indian Penal Code, pending in the Court of the Additional Judicial Commissioner-XVIII-cum-Special Judge, C.I.D., Ranchi.

He is also a Secretary of an NGO.
He stated that a huge fraud has been committed by Sahara India Ltd. and its directors and officials including this petitioner.
To facilitate the said fraud, companies like Sahara India Real Estate Ltd. and Sahara Housing Investment Corporation Ltd. was established.
The entire operation was being controlled by Subrata Roy, his family members and other close associates.
These firms and companies amassed huge money from public.

sentences.text: (vii) Sahara India Commercial Cooperation Ltd.
These companies 2025:JHHC:22275 started collecting money with an aim to commit fraud.
Investments were taken from common people and the money was swindled.
These companies did not have office of their own, but, operated from the office of Sahara India and the agents of Sahara India worked for them.
Informant further stated that his wife had invested Rs.90 lakh in Sahara India from 2008 to 2021 in Fixed Deposit, and on maturity, about Rs.1.3 crore was to be paid, but the money was embezzled.
In August 2023, a Central Cooperative Sahara Refund Portal was created.

The petitioner had claimed through the said portal, but all the claims were rejected, intimating that the petitioner's wife was not member of the Society, and the petitioner was asked to contact the office, but all the offices of Sahara were closed.
Informant has the certificates, Pass Books etc. with their seal, but the money has not been paid.
He submits that there are several other victims and this petitioner along with others are persons who in a planned manner have duped the public at large including the informant.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is one of the directors and wife of the informant was also an agent and she has also been paid some amount as commission.
He further submitted that the petitioner being an employee of BCCL cannot float an NGO.
It is his further contention that the entire dispute is civil in nature and Sahara India has already refunded more than Rs.2000 crore Pan India through their portal.
The wife of the informant has also committed fraud with the Society, as none of the investments submitted by her was proper, rather were deposited with fake documents.
He lastly submitted that this case has been filed only to take refund of the amount, which according to the informant is allegedly invested by his wife.
4. Learned counsel for the State as also the learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer of the petitioner for grant of anticipatory bail.
They submitted that the petitioner is the Executive Director in a Society and Director in other companies, through which money was looted.
He submits that inspite of order from the appropriate authority, the company accepted deposits and collected money.
It is his contention that for refund of the money deposited by the petitioner's wife, claim was made, but their claim was rejected on the ground that their name does not figure as depositors.
This is a fraud committed by the accused persons and others.

They submitted that this is a case of extensive investigation in presence of the petitioner as without interrogating the petitioner, the magnitude of the fraud and the link and money trail cannot be unearthed.
From the arguments of the parties, I find that this case has been registered for offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420, 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
There is an allegation that huge investment was made by the wife of the petitioner and return was not paid.
There is an allegation that by floating companies, money has been diverted.
Petitioner is admittedly a Director of Sahara Credit Cooperative Society Ltd. and was Territorial Head of State of Bihar and Jharkhand.

sentences.text: 2 the said money was siphoned and was channelized through different societies and thereafter has been misappropriated.
Further, I find that this is not a simple case of non- refund of maturity value of any deposit, but deep down, there is an allegation of diverting money through different cooperative societies.
This large scale diversion of money and misappropriation needs extensive investigation.
Not only the accused needs to be interrogated, but electronic devices, which are in control of the accused persons also need to be scrutinized.

There is also an allegation that when the informant's wife got herself registered on the portal for refund, she was intimated that there is no such membership which suggests element of fraud as it is the case of the informant that wife of the informant had invested money, but the same was not returned.

Further from the case diary, at paragraph 148, I find that notice under Section 35(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita was issued to the petitioner, but the same has not been complied with, thus, warrant of arrest has also been issued.
In the case diary, there are materials to suggest that the petitioner was at helm of affairs of these companies and societies through which money was diverted.

6. Considering the aforesaid facts, as this is not only a case of non- refund of maturity value, but large element of economic offence is involved, which needs extensive investigation and investigation in presence of this petitioner also, this is not a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
I am not inclined to grant privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
The prayer for grant of anticipatory bail of the petitioner, abovenamed, is hereby rejected.
7. This anticipatory bail application is, accordingly, dismissed.
